messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: elevated GPU OOMs and token errors on eu-west-1 pool starting 1777770000. Error rate spike ~8% vs baseline 0.3%. paging oncall rotation. automated mitigation suggestions: reduce concurrency, adjust batching window, apply soft rate limits. https://alerts.redwood.internal/INC-20260315-221

arjun: acked. I'm oncall. seeing same in metrics. p99 latency up ~2x and error surge coincides with a traffic spike from customer tenant 'acme-ml' (heavy long-context jobs).

maria: @arjun good catch — acme-ml started a large ingestion 5m ago, many long seqs. do we want to throttle that tenant first?

arjun: yes let's do tenant-level throttle and try batching tuning. priority is to stop OOMs, even if latency increases for some.

lee: suggest steps: 1) apply temporary quota cap on acme-ml (requests/s down to 20) 2) increase continuous_batch_window from 50ms -> 250ms for eu-west-1 shared pool 3) lower max_concurrent_inference_per_gpu from 80 -> 40. any objections?

zara: no objections. are we sure increasing batch window will help OOMs? want to avoid head-of-line blocking for other tenants.

arjun: increasing batch window should increase batch packing, reducing per-request memory peak. tradeoff is higher tail latency. acceptable for this mitigation window. we'll monitor for head-of-line.

arjun: performing step 1 now: applying tenant quota for acme-ml. command: 
```
# admin-cli
tenant throttle set --tenant acme-ml --rps 20 --duration 30m --reason "live incident mitigation"
```

oncall-bot: ACTION: tenant throttle applied for acme-ml (20 rps) by arjun at 1777770065.

lee: applying batching change on config-service: updating continuous_batch_window to 250ms for eu-west-1 pool. patch posted: `patch /configs/runtime/eu-west-1`

maria: copying the exact mutation for audit: 
```
PATCH /configs/runtime/eu-west-1
{
  "continuous_batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "batch_window_ms": 250,
    "max_batch_size": 64
  }
}
```

ops-bot: KICKOFF: rolling config restart of runtime agents in eu-west-1 (graceful) — 12 nodes, 2 at a time. Estimated 6m.

arjun: lowering gpu concurrency now: 
```
admin-cli cluster set --pool eu-west-1 --max_concurrent_per_gpu 40
```

lee: quick note: I'm also enabling a soft rate limit on anonymous/free-tier routes to reduce background noise: 10 rps global.

maria: metrics update (1777770120): GPU OOMs down from 8% -> 1.6% after tenant throttle and first few nodes restarted. error rate trending down. p95 latency increased ~180ms for some routes (expected).

zara: any customer impact notes? acme-ml support pinged earlier. I told them we applied a temporary ingest cap and to expect higher latency but fewer failures.

arjun: will send CSE note. Also opening a follow-up: revert plan and post-incident action items. We need a safer long-term mitigation: model-specific quantization or dedicated capacity for heavy-long-context tenants.

oncall-bot: UPDATE: rolling config rollout complete at 1777770300. all 12 nodes updated.

maria: confirm final health (1777770340): OOMs <0.5%, token error rate back near baseline, throughput stabilized albeit at ~70% of pre-incident due to narrower concurrency and bigger batches.

arjun: ok wrap: keeping tenant throttle for 30m as scheduled, batch_window will stay at 250ms for now while we evaluate. action items: (1) SRE to run load test with batch_window=250ms to validate head-of-line impacts (lee) (2) Product to contact acme-ml about dedicated capacity offer (zara) (3) Eng-ML evaluate quantization/kv-cache improvements (maria). I'll hand over to next oncall at 1777770360.

lee: thanks — handoff acknowledged. I'll keep an eye on dashboards for 1hr. :thumbsup:
